page.overview:
Who is Alexander Albon?

Alexander Philippe Albon Ansusinha "Alex" (born 23 March 1996) is an Anglo-Thai racing driver, racing under the Thai flag, who is currently competing in Formula 1 for Williams. Albon made his debut during the season for Toro Rosso.

Albon was a former member of the Red Bull Junior Team, but was dropped in 2012 after a difficult year in Formula Renault. However, after a series of driver changes prior to the 2019 edition of F1, Albon was asked to rejoin the Red Bull family in place of Brendon Hartley at their junior F1 team.

During the 2019 mid-season break, it was announced that Albon would replace Pierre Gasly at Red Bull, with the Thai driver making his Red Bull debut at the 2019 Belgian Grand Prix. However, during his partnership with Max Verstappen, he struggled to match his performance, and after scoring two podiums in 2020, he was dropped to a reserve role in 2021. Albon returned to the grid in the 2022 season for Williams.

Albon, the son of Nigel Albon, an ex-racer in the British Touring Car Championship, began his karting career at the age of eight, winning his local Championship in the Cadet class. The following seasons would see Albon compete in higher capacity classes at a national level, before ultimately finishing as runner up in the CIK-FIA World Championship in 2011. That latter triumph earned Albon a role in the Red Bull Junior Team for 2012, with the Anglo-Thai racer moving into single seaters for the year.
